title: I built a library of trading automations for monitoring, alerts, and trade management
author: Obside_AI
selftext:
I've been working on a trading agent library (as part of a product we're building).

The idea is pretty simple: instead of having to build every trading automation from scratch, traders can pick a ready-made agent, customize it, and run it on a connected broker.

The automations are mostly focused on boring/repetitive things that traders or investors would otherwise have to check manually.

A few examples we've built so far:

* **Position Exit Manager:** monitors open positions every minute and can move a (trailing) stop loss to a level you define once a certain profit threshold is reached.
* **Portfolio Concentration Monitor:** watches portfolio exposure and alerts you if a position or sector becomes too concentrated.
* **13F Whale Watcher:** checks new SEC 13F filings and notifies you when it detects new institutional investments in a stock.
* **Economic Event Brief:** follows economic events like CPI, jobs data, Fed/ECB meetings, etc. and sends reminders/digests beforehand based on what you're exposed to.

There are around 20 automations available right now, covering monitoring, alerts, portfolio management and trade management. More will be added.

Users can also create their own agents and share them in the library for other people to use or customize.

The part I'm particularly interested in is figuring out which automations are actually useful enough that people would leave them running 24/7.

There are lots of things I could build, but I'd rather make agents around problems traders actually have.

So I'm curious:

**If you could have one trading/investing task running automatically in the background, what would you want it to do?**

Could be something very simple too. Price/indicator alerts, monitoring a setup across 50 assets, earnings/news monitoring, managing stops, detecting unusual activity, portfolio risk, etc.

I'm looking for ideas, including weird/niche ones 😄

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
I'd leave a protective-order watchdog running: check whether each open position actually has the intended stop at the broker, and flag missing protection or a stop quantity that no longer matches after a partial fill or manual trade.

Your Position Exit Manager checks every minute, and the screenshot shows “Armed,” “Exit sent,” and “Executed.” A separate “broker stop confirmed” state would help distinguish an agent watching a threshold from an order resting at the broker. A useful demo would be cancelling the stop directly in the broker and showing how quickly the agent notices. Does protection remain active if the agent disconnects?

replies.author: Obside_AI
replies.body:
Thanks for your input!
At the moment the agent immediately sends the exit order to the broker (or with user approval first if selected) once the trailing level is touched. If somehow the agent disconnects, the user would be instantly notified.

comments.author: artguerilla
comments.body: I'm currently trying to get a trading bot running 24/7 with different strats but especially dip detection and sudden changes in market while scalp trading is really giving me a hard time. Latency is key i guess. Things like JEV help alot. I also use forcasting to have some probabilty of how the chart may move next.

comments.author: MoralMechanics
comments.body: The boring automations are probably the most valuable ones Concentration checks event reminders stop management and monitoring fifty symbols are exactly the things people forget when nothing exciting is happening I would prioritize portfolio level risk controls over another signal generator If Moon ever gets plugged into this kind of automation stack a simple wager risk monitor would honestly be more useful than an AI trying to predict every tick
